SNV Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship AET Zambia 2024-2028

description.narrative: Projektet YEE AET Zambia har som mål att öka antalet jobb för unga människor, särskilt unga kvinnor, inom livsmedelsindustrin och bidra till företagsutveckling genom ökad handel i Zambia. De specifika målen är att: (1) Öka handelsmöjligheterna för unga människor, även inom klimatresilienta livsmedelsvärdekedjor; (2) Öka ungas tillgång till formella anställningsmöjligheter; och (3) förbättra stödet för ökad jämställdhet och inkludering av ungdomar genom policyramverk. Projektets slutmål är att bidra till att öka sysselsättnings-, entreprenörs- och handelsmöjligheterna så att unga zambiska män och kvinnor får bättre och mer motståndskraftiga försörjningsmöjligheter.

The YEE AET Zambia project aims to increase jobs for young people, particularly young women, in the agri-food industry and contribute to enterprise growth through increased trade in Zambia. The specific objectives are to: (1) Increase trading opportunities for young people, also in climate resilient in high value agri-food value-chains; (2) Increase young people access to decent (self) employment; and (3) Improve policy support and market decisions for increased gender equality and youth inclusion. The end goal of the project is to contribute to increase the employment, entrepreneurial and trade opportunities so that young Zambian men and women have better and more resilient livelihoods.

title.narrative: SNV Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship AET Zambia
SNV Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship AET Zambia

description.narrative:
During the period January-June 2025, the Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship (YEE) Phase II programme made some progress and accelerated delivery across Zimbabwe and Zambia, despite earlier delays in donor on boarding.
The SNV Youth Employment and Entrepreneurship (YEE) Phase II programme is creating better conditions for livelihoods and trade through climate-smart, inclusive agriculture and entrepreneurship for youths. In the first half of 2025, the programme scaled delivery significantly, training 4392 (2325 female, 2067 male) youth in life and business skills and 1088 (593 female, 494 male) in technical areas such as horticulture, poultry, renewable energy, and agro processing. It facilitated access to finance for 100 youth (71 female, 29 male), catalysing nearly 307 enterprises, and supported over 880 youth transitions into employment. Rapid expansion of Youth Savings and Lending Schemes and digital innovations, alongside policy engagement to unlock land, finance, and market access, are embedding sustainable models for youth economic empowerment. These achievements strengthen productive, climate-smart livelihoods and contribute towards reducing poverty among young people in Zambia.
**Update by AGK, 10 March 2026: please note that these numbers are for the YEE program at large, combining results from Zambia and Zimbabwe. The semi-annual report does not divide results by country. SNV has been tasked to provide more specific results on Zambia in the upcoming annual report.
Several unexpected results emerged that reinforced the programmes resilience such as digital innovations, particularly the digital literacy pilot in Zambia exceeded early expectations by reaching 1,284 youth and demonstrating strong uptake among rural participants. The youth champion model expanded peertopeer mobilisation, with 361 champions driving local engagement, mentorship, and behaviour change beyond planned levels. Emerging green and export oriented enterprises, such as the Macheke horticulture export pilot, generated higher-than-anticipated employment multipliers, demonstrating the programmes potential to stimulate jobs in highvalue niches. Despite macroeconomic volatility in Zimbabwe and donor transitions in Zambia, the programme has built strong momentum, with clear evidence that acceleration measures, cascading training models, and strengthened private sector linkages are enabling the programme to catch up on initial delays and position itself to achieve 2025 milestones and longer term outcomes.
